subsystems.name: Minimal genome
subsystems.role: the smallest set of genes that can sustain growth and division.
parts: control elements that set when each gene is read

subsystems.name: Envelope
subsystems.role: contains the reaction mixture and separates it from the outside.
parts: an emptied bacterial cell shell (top-down route)

subsystems.name: Cytoplasm and machinery
subsystems.role: the soluble apparatus that reads genes and makes proteins.

subsystems.name: Energy and building blocks
subsystems.role: supplies the ATP and small molecules needed for growth.
parts: amino acid, nucleotide and lipid supply

subsystems.name: Growth and division module
subsystems.role: turns a static vesicle into something that copies itself and splits.

subsystems.name: Analysis layer
subsystems.role: works out which parts are truly needed.

buildSteps.title: Design a candidate gene set
buildSteps.detail: Compare the genomes of closely related bacteria to list every gene likely to be required, and flag the ones already known to be disposable.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise the genome
buildSteps.detail: Short DNA strands are built chemically and joined in overlapping pieces into a full circular genome, then error-checked by sequencing.

buildSteps.title: Transplant or encapsulate
buildSteps.detail: Top-down: insert the genome into a cell whose own DNA has been removed. Bottom-up: enclose purified machinery inside a lipid vesicle a few micrometres across.

buildSteps.title: Boot the cell
buildSteps.detail: Confirm the new genome is read and the cell grows, rather than remaining dormant.

buildSteps.title: Compress the genome
buildSteps.detail: Delete genes one at a time or in blocks and measure growth after each cut, keeping only what the cell cannot live without.

buildSteps.title: Restore what broke
buildSteps.detail: Genes initially classed as non-essential often prove necessary once removed; add them back and re-test. In the 473-gene minimal cell reported in 2016, roughly a third of the genes had no known function.

buildSteps.title: Fix growth defects
buildSteps.detail: Minimal cells tend to grow slowly and divide unevenly; adjust gene dosage, membrane composition and medium to get robust, uniform division.

buildSteps.title: Make it self-sufficient
buildSteps.detail: Replace supplied nutrients and cofactors step by step with reactions the cell performs itself, until it grows on a simple defined medium.

buildSteps.title: Prove it is defined
buildSteps.detail: Sequence and assay the final cell to show that every component is known, and that it grows and divides reliably over many generations.

prerequisites.why: a whole bacterial genome must be built chemically, base by base, and assembled without errors.
a synthesised genome has to be moved into a working cell envelope and take control of it.
without genome-wide tests of which genes can be deleted, there is no way to find the minimum.
the bottom-up route needs purified machinery that makes proteins outside a living cell.

prerequisites.tech: Membrane growth and division from defined molecules
prerequisites.why: no artificial vesicle has yet been shown to synthesise its own membrane and split on a defined chemical recipe.
designing a genome from scratch requires predicting the behaviour of the whole system, not single genes.

pathway.milestone: bacteria with reduced genomes used to catalogue essential genes and as simplified research chassis
pathway.unlocks: a working list of the genes life actually needs.

pathway.milestone: fully synthesised minimal genomes with every remaining gene assigned a role
pathway.unlocks: cells whose behaviour can be predicted from their sequence.

pathway.milestone: a synthetic minimal genome operating inside an artificial envelope
pathway.unlocks: hybrid cells that combine designed genes with designed containers.

pathway.milestone: vesicles that grow and divide on a defined chemical medium
pathway.unlocks: a genuine bottom-up cell and a test of what life minimally requires.
predictable, contained production strains with no spare genetic baggage.
